rationale: Zero-ask approver regression check on 27294e84 in the decomposition lens: clean. The round-4 fix touches only bead 6 (protocol restated as the M/R/S/G/T staged state machine with two-ref update-ref --stdin transactions; steps 1/4/5 rewritten; fixtures ix/x/xi added) and bead 1/lock-home wording (stale O_EXCL framings swept — a pure consistency fix with no seam impact). No depends_on changed in any of the five commits — frontmatter still exactly matches all ten sections. Chunk/section parity for the new material: every edit site the staged machinery names maps to files chunk 6 already lists (commit-tree builders and the transaction helper in internal/gitutil beside recordMergeSourceMarker — gitops.go/snapshot.go; the early sequence and staged flow in complete.go; fixtures ix-xi in complete_test.go; the extended amendment in ADR-0041 + its test); no new file names were introduced anywhere in the diff. On the lead's central question — bead 6's size — my judgment is ACCEPTABLE-BUT-LARGE, keep whole, with the rationale recorded as a finding rather than a block: the strongest argument is empirical, from this very panel's history. The two real protocol bugs the gate caught (round-2's synthetic artifact deletion, round-2's phantom staged deletions) both lived in the SEAM between primitive semantics and consumer expectation — exactly the class a primitives-only bead 6a reviewed apart from its consumer would miss. The bead's invariants (committed==measured; marker==tip by construction; plain-re-run converges at every kill point) are properties of the whole machine, and its eleven-leg kill/failure fixture matrix is the reviewability instrument that lets a single panel judge it. A split would buy one smaller PR at the cost of a serial-cycle round AND a review boundary drawn through the protocol's known bug habitat.

findings.title: Bead 6: acceptable-but-large — keep whole (final size judgment, with rationale)
findings.detail: Final scope: snapshot primitive, two commit-tree builders, the two-ref transaction helper, executor tree leg + tree-grounded input reads, both gates' snapshot legs, complete.go's early sequence + staged M/R/S/G/T machine replacing two porcelain paths, the ADR-0041 amendment, and eleven fixture legs plus the cross-checkout test. This is the plan's heaviest bead and sits at the upper bound of single-PR reviewability, but the split candidate (6a = gitutil/executor primitives, 6b = complete-flow + ADR + fixtures) draws the review boundary exactly where this gate's own five rounds found the real bugs: the synthetic-artifact-deletion and phantom-staged-deletion defects were both primitive-vs-consumer seam bugs, discovered because the protocol was reviewed as one unit. The invariants are whole-machine properties; the kill matrix (fixtures viii-xi + failure legs i-vii) gives the bead panel a complete falsification instrument. The serial-cycle cost of an extra bead buys no reviewability that the fixture matrix does not already provide. Judgment: keep whole. One editorial nit, not worth a round: step 4 still says 'reconcile path untouched' while stage T now clears the marker on the landed-merge-reconcile completion path and the early sequence adds reconcile-detection-first — 'untouched' is true of the reconcile MEASUREMENT (M^1..M) but no longer of the path in the strictest sense; the protocol paragraph states the actual behavior explicitly, so no ambiguity survives for an implementer.
